claims.text: High-temperature annealing produces homogeneous, random solid-solution Al0.1CrCoFeNi nanoparticles.
Rapid quenching kinetically traps the random solid-solution structure.
Kinetic trapping inhibits thermally activated ordering or phase separation during operation from 473 to 1923 K.
Slow cooling provides sufficient atomic mobility for structural and chemical rearrangement.
Slowly cooled nanoparticles rearrange into thermodynamically favored ordered or compositionally segregated phases.
Formation of ordered or segregated phases compromises structural and chemical stability.
Rapid quenching minimizes atomic diffusion by freezing the high-configurational-entropy state.
Reduced diffusion during quenching preserves the random solid solution.
Diffusion during slow cooling enables local ordering or phase separation.
Local ordering or phase separation undermines catalytic or thermoelectric performance.
Rapidly quenched nanoparticles will retain uniform lattice parameters during thermal cycling.
Rapidly quenched nanoparticles will retain a random, spatially uniform elemental distribution.
Rapidly quenched nanoparticles will maintain stable catalytic and thermoelectric performance.
Slowly cooled nanoparticles will exhibit ordering or phase segregation during thermal cycling.
Ordering or phase segregation in slowly cooled nanoparticles will be accompanied by diminished performance.
An inert atmosphere precludes oxidation and other chemical interferences relevant to the comparison.
Kinetically trapped nanoparticles may reconfigure during sufficiently long exposure at the highest operating temperatures.
